archetypes.name: regression-coverage-gap
archetypes.rationale: The harness drops ~1900 lines of contract checks (Step 0-pre/0b route/init/degraded block assertions, postplan thin-fence self-tests, gate-b bypass sentinels, step3b diagram branches, publish fence guards, step2a simple guard, etc.). The plan says these move to wrapper-specific tests, but the diff must be verified to either include those replacement checks or explicitly defer them to a follow-on harness.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the net deletion in scripts/test-design-structure.sh: identify which previously-asserted contracts (Step 0-pre argv block, Step 0b route/init block, degraded-tools gate fence, postplan thin-fence, step2a SIMPLE guard, gate-b bypass sentinels, Step 3b diagram branches, publish fence guards, Step 5c sidecar write, etc.) are no longer checked by any file in this diff. For each deleted assertion, determine whether a replacement check appears in any new or modified file in this diff, or whether the contract is now entirely unguarded. Flag any contract that was previously machine-enforced and is now only documented in prose or not present at all. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: kv-contract-drift
archetypes.rationale: Every new design-step*.sh wrapper emits specific stdout KV names that SKILL.md (or downstream wrappers) must bind before branches. A single name mismatch (e.g. STEP0_STATUS vs STEP_0_STATUS, or missing PUBLISH_RC on rc=4) silently breaks routing. The plan enumerates required allowlists but the diff must be checked for drift between emitted names, consumed names, and the plan's specified allowlists.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each new wrapper script in skills/design/scripts/ that appears in this diff, check whether the KV names it is specified to emit in plan.txt (stdout contract sections) appear to be consumed under the same exact names in SKILL.md fences or downstream wrappers. Pay particular attention to design-step0.sh (STEP0_STATUS, POSITIONAL_KIND, ROUTE values), design-step2b-postplan.sh (POSTPLAN_STATUS, POSTPLAN_RC, VALIDATE_* names), design-step5c.sh (rc=4 validator-defect handoff keys, PLAN_WRITE_OK), and design-step6.sh (.design-step5c-status.env allowlist). Also check whether the new assert_design_skill_bash_fences_are_wrappers regex pattern in test-design-structure.sh correctly accepts all the intended fence shapes (e.g. fences with <PUBLIC_ARGV_WORDS>, multi-line continuations, optional flags) without false positives or false negatives. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: pause-sentinel-ordering
archetypes.rationale: Every post-Step-1c direct-called wrapper must source session env and run pause-check before performing any real work. Sentinel writes must occur in the correct order relative to pause-check (before for most steps, after only for step-6). These invariants are easy to violate silently and were previously enforced by assert_bash_fences_have_pause_check and assert_folded_sentinel_writes — both of which are deleted in this diff.
archetypes.prompt_body: For each new design-step*.sh wrapper script visible in this diff, verify that: (1) the script sources session env before performing any work (exempting only the pre-setup phase of design-step0.sh --phase initial), (2) pause-check runs before any substantive work (not after), (3) sentinel writes that are required before pause-check (e.g. step-1c, step-1d in design-step0-ap-continue.sh; step-3.5 in design-step3b-entry.sh) appear before the pause-save call, and (4) the step-6 sentinel is explicitly documented to write after pause-check. Also check whether the new assert_design_skill_wrapper_contracts function in test-design-structure.sh actually enforces these ordering requirements or merely checks for file existence. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
